slides.title: 1. WX-4 tablets: stability review
slides.subtitle: Wexanthel Medicines | {{PRJ0088:project_id}} | 26 Jan 2017
bullets: QA-approved client readout | Dr A. Penrose
ICH chamber programme and Assay and related-substances validation
slides.notes: Final readout. Protocol opened 22 Jul 2015; approved results completed 23 Jan 2017. LIMS accession {{PRJ0088:lims_id}}. The qualified method detected a packaging-dependent impurity trend. Wexanthel adopted the higher-barrier blister.

slides.title: 2. Approved numerical evidence
slides.notes: Source: E-004 / WX4_PULLS_AND_SUITABILITY_RESULTS_Rev03.xlsx, approved 23 Jan 2017. Assay is percent label claim; total impurities are area percent. Condition and pull interval remain part of each result identity. Individual impurities and water results are retained in the full sequence sheets.

slides.title: 3. Protocol identity and sample custody
bullets: Dr L. Wu: stability lot and sample-custody reconciliation.
bullets_right: Storage condition and pull interval are carried with the stability lot on the batch card.
Sequence sheets retain the pack or presentation identity; results must not be pooled across storage conditions.
slides.notes: The accession links receipt, batch card, preparation and analytical sequence. This readout does not introduce new lot codes or replace approved sequence sheets.

slides.title: 4. HPLC method qualification
slides.notes: Saira Mahmood, QC Method Validation Lead: qualification review. Read each result against its stated acceptance criterion. Assay and related-substances validation supports the reported sample preparation and separation; extensions require a separately agreed protocol.

slides.title: 5. Impurity trend by storage interval
slides.notes: The qualified method detected a packaging-dependent impurity trend. The plot is a view of the approved stability table; the table supplies condition, interval and compliance status. Do not extrapolate beyond {{PRJ0088:stability.last_timepoint_months}} months.

slides.title: 6. System suitability and deviation disposition
bullets: Saira Mahmood: analytical method and system suitability review.
Dr L. Wu: reconciliation of preparation, storage and sequence identity.
Dr A. Penrose: approved interpretation and client release.
bullets_right: Approved sequence sheets are the authority for suitability acceptance and any repeat sequence.
Deviation notes remain linked to the affected batch card; this deck does not replace their disposition.
No additional chamber excursion, reinjection or acceptance limit is inferred from the trend plot.
slides.notes: Readout source: WX4_PULLS_AND_SUITABILITY_RESULTS_Rev03.xlsx. Distinguish an observed formulation or packaging effect from an analytical deviation. The qualified method detected a packaging-dependent impurity trend.

slides.title: 7. Interpretation for transfer
bullets: The qualified method detected a packaging-dependent impurity trend.
Carry the higher-barrier blister into transfer; keep the packaging comparison attached to the stability lot history.
Conclusion applies to tested storage conditions and the reported {{PRJ0088:stability.last_timepoint_months}}-month interval.
slides.notes: The packaging decision follows the impurity trend detected by the qualified method. Do not recast that trend as a generic analytical failure.

slides.title: 8. Release gate and client decision
bullets: Carry the higher-barrier blister into transfer; keep the packaging comparison attached to the stability lot history.
Archive the approved readout with the sequence sheets, batch cards and linked deviation notes.
slides.notes: Dr A. Penrose | Head of Analytical Services | 26 Jan 2017. Final client readout for Wexanthel Medicines. Later shelf-life conclusions require additional approved pulls.
